# Harrison

## Overview

- **Age:** Middle-aged (fifty-five)  <sub>[v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v2 c25 P16](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0016)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick (Scottsford)  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** J. A. Harrison  <sub>[v2 c1 P1](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0001)</sub>; A crank  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Harrison is a short, fat, bald man with a round face, prominent blue eyes, and a fringe of hair around his ears. He is generally unkempt, sometimes going unshaved and wearing patched or torn working clothes, though he trims his hair and shaves when tidied up by his wife. He is noted for his lack of outward physical comeliness.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c1 P21](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0021), [v2 c25 P46](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0046), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)_

## Personality

Mr. Harrison is blunt, outspoken, and quick-tempered, often blurting out disagreeable truths without regard for diplomatic tact. Despite his irritable exterior and reputation as a crank, he is at heart kindly, fond of company, and possesses a latent sense of humor. He enjoys smoking his pipe, chatting with young people, and holding strong opinions, particularly against gossips like Mrs. Rachel Lynde.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P25](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0025), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049), [v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000), [v2 c9 P9](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0009)_

- Blunt and outspoken  <sub>[v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025)</sub>

- Brewing tea  <sub>[v2 c3 P31](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0031)</sub>

## Goals

- To live a quiet, comfortable life free from nagging and fussiness  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>

## History

After moving to Avonlea from New Brunswick, Mr. Harrison quickly gained a reputation as an eccentric bachelor and crank due to his unusual housekeeping habits and outspoken nature. His relationship with his neighbor, Anne Shirley, began on a stormy note when Anne's Jersey cow broke into his oatfield, leading to an angry confrontation. Shortly after, Anne accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's own Jersey cow to a buyer, mistaking it for her own. When she went to his house to confess, Mr. Harrison received the news with surprising good humor, accepted Anne's cow in exchange, and invited her to tea, beginning a warm friendship between them. He supported the Avonlea Village Improvement Society in its endeavors, though he refused to give financial subscriptions. Following a false rumor published in a local newspaper that he was courting a local woman, his estranged wife, Emily, arrived at his home in Avonlea. The two reconciled, as the parrot Ginger—the original cause of their separation—had died, and Mrs. Harrison took charge of his household, bringing neatness and order back into his life.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013), [v2 c2 P35](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0035), [v2 c3 P21](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0021), [v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P31](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0031), [v2 c3 P40](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0040), [v2 c24 P2](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0002), [v2 c24 P43](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0043), [v2 c25 P15](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0015), [v2 c25 P47](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0047), [v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059)_

## Background by volume

- Lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, where his sister kept house for him until her death.  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Promised his dying sister he would marry Emily Scott, whom he subsequently married.  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Separated from his wife Emily after a quarrel over his parrot, Ginger, and moved to Avonlea.  <sub>[v2 c25 P58](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0058), [v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059)</sub>
- Bought Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea, adjoining Green Gables on the west.  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Quotes

> I'm a terrible outspoken old fellow, that's all . . . awful apt to tell the truth, no matter if it is a bit plain.  <sub>[v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025)</sub>

> Bless my soul, what's that redheaded snippet coming here for?  <sub>[v2 c3 P4](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0004)</sub>

> I'm a crusty, lonesome, crabbed old chap, but there's something about that little girl makes me feel young again.  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

> Spare the rod and spoil the child.  <sub>[v2 c4 P36](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0036)</sub>
